_reviewProof: 2026-08-01: proof of review moved from hand-written marker files to the RECORDED ledger. A marker is a separate act of writing performed by the party being audited â€” twelve such writes were flagged as forged in Butlery on 2026-08-01, and every stricter spelling of the assertion (name the file, pin the sha, list what you read) was still an assertion. In ledger mode a PostToolUse hook records which reviewer read which bytes and a SubagentStop hook records the verdict it ended on; nothing is hand-writable, and a later fix silently un-proves the file it touched. This repo's four agents already pinned shas honestly, so this is a hardening rather than a repair. All four carry the two rules it depends on: open files with Read, and end on REVIEW-VERDICT: pass|fail (N blocking).

WHY IT IS REVIEW MACHINERY, in the same sense as its neighbours: `npm run lint` fails on this rule and CI runs `npm run lint`, so weakening the rule weakens a check that refuses commits. Its provenance makes that sharper — it REPLACED four regex source scans plus two absence tests that lived inside functions/src/streamingOffers/backfillIds.test.ts, a file the repo-wide `\.test\.(ts|tsx)$` test-gate pattern already stopped. Moving that guard out of the test tree and into eslint-rules/ would have moved it out of review in the same edit, with nothing saying so. HOW THE GAP WAS NAMED, stated accurately because two of the notes above had to be corrected for flattering themselves on exactly this point: route.test.mjs's BIN-874 discovery half went red the moment 'eslint-rules/**/*.{test,spec}.mjs' was added to vitest.config.ts's include globs, naming both files by path. This note used to end by recording eslint.config.mjs as deliberately NOT added, with the red test priced as the weaker guarantee that replaced a reviewer. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-23 by BIN-967 — the file IS added, and _note12 is the dated successor carrying that decision and its re-measured cost. Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note14: 2026-08-25, BIN-998: the TWELFTH widening — docs/org/rules-doc-id-symmetry.test.mjs, folded into the existing tooling alternation rather than given a pattern of its own, because it sits under docs/org/ alongside route and gate-symmetry, and a second spelling of one class inside one gate is a second place to look. Added in the SAME commit as its TOOLING_CODE_FILES entry in docs/org/route.mjs — the BIN-830 rule applied at authoring time rather than days later. WHY IT IS REVIEW MACHINERY: it is the only mechanism holding firestore.rules' two deliberate copies of the document-id shape rule (canonicalWatchlistDocId in the watchlist block, canonicalSwipeDocId in the sessions block) byte-identical. Before it, that invariant existed only as prose. STRUCK 2026-08-25 before commit, by this change's own outcome verifier: this sentence first restated the ticket's measurement as 'grepping the two helper names across src/docs/scripts outside test files returned zero hits', which drops the `--include=*.ts --include=*.mjs` filter the ticket actually ran with and is false without it -- `grep -rnE 'canonicalWatchlistDocId|canonicalSwipeDocId' src docs scripts` minus its test-file hits returns one hit, docs/workflow-map.html, where both guards are described in prose. No count is written in its place: outside firestore.rules and its own tests the two names appear only in prose, which is exactly the state that made a mechanism necessary. Recorded rather than silently reworded because an unmeasured number inside a note about measured claims is this repo's most-repeated defect. Weakening or deleting the check re-opens the silent state BIN-797 closed by hand. HOW THE PLACEMENT WAS DECIDED, said plainly because a role got it wrong and the correction is the useful part: the full panel split. #21 Technical Writer required it be an it() inside src/test/rules/firestore-rules.test.ts, on the stated ground that the file is already collected by the main vitest run. That is false, and it was settled by reading the config rather than by argument — vitest.config.ts carries exclude: ['node_modules', '.next', 'out', 'src/test/rules/**'], so that directory runs ONLY under `npm run test:rules`, behind the Firestore emulator and a Java install, as a separate CI job. #25 Engineering Manager and #27 DBA both required the opposite — that the guard live where `npm test` actually runs it — and the measurement says they are right. It is therefore a plain *.test.mjs under docs/org/, caught by the pre-existing include glob docs/org/**/*.{test,spec}.mjs, with no vitest.config.ts edit needed. Being a plain test rather than a check-*.mjs CLI it also needs no entry in scripts/scripts-self-tests-present.test.mjs's REQUIRED floor — #4 Security Architect's condition 5 named that case and is void by the branch taken. PROVEN, not asserted: three mutations of firestore.rules were applied one at a time, each asserted present by `git hash-object` BEFORE and AFTER its suite run, each restored from a scratchpad snapshot, and the file re-verified byte-identical to HEAD (63c5daf0055e3b5b71d7e18ca0153abf0df7cbb1) at the end. Narrowing only the swipe copy: 1 failed of 4. Renaming canonicalSwipeDocId: 3 failed of 4. Replacing the watchlist body with `return true`: 2 failed of 4. The count floor is asserted BEFORE any comparison, so an extraction regex that stops matching fails loudly instead of comparing nothing to nothing. firestore.rules itself is unmodified by this commit. Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note15: 2026-08-28, BIN-1002: the THIRTEENTH widening — docs/org/rules-id-client-symmetry.test.mjs, folded into the same tooling alternation as its BIN-998 sibling for the same reason (one class, one spelling, one place to look). Added in the SAME commit as its TOOLING_CODE_FILES entry in docs/org/route.mjs, per BIN-830. WHY IT IS REVIEW MACHINERY: _note14 above records the sibling as holding firestore.rules two deliberate copies of the id-shape rule identical to EACH OTHER. This one holds that rule against the ids the CLIENT actually builds, which is the invariant that decides whether real writes go through — drift there means the app writes ids the rules refuse, or the rules admit shapes the app cannot read back. That is BIN-797 exactly (movie_0 written by the sweep, then refused by the client), and BIN-560/618/766/931/932 are the same family. HOW IT AVOIDS BEING A THIRD COPY OF THE RULE: it restates neither side. The rules regex is extracted from firestore.rules as text, and the client verdict comes from CALLING the real mediaTypeDocId and parseTmdbIdFromDocId — a .mjs test can import the TypeScript module under vitest, established by a throwaway probe before the file was written, not assumed. The cases are generated across the boundaries the two sides have actually disagreed about before (0, 042, empty suffix, negative, non-integer) rather than hand-listed, which is the change the ticket asked for: a hand-written example proves only that the example works. PROVEN, not asserted: CANONICAL_TMDB_ID in src/lib/mediaTypeDocId.ts was widened to /^[0-9]+$/, the mutant asserted present BEFORE and AFTER the suite run in one command, the agreement test failed, and the file was restored from a git-show snapshot and re-verified by git hash-object against its pre-mutation hash. Three floors are asserted BEFORE any agreement is compared — that a pattern was extracted at all, that the corpus did not collapse, and that BOTH an accepted and a refused case exist — so an extraction that stops matching fails loudly instead of comparing nothing to nothing. firestore.rules is unmodified by this commit. It claims nothing about the update path (both rules blocks guard ids on CREATE only, deliberately) and nothing about legacy bare-id documents (mediaTypeDocId never emits one). Widening only; nothing was removed.
